propositions: The overlap judge re-sends the query ticket digest in every per-call user message instead of caching it in the stable system prefix, causing repetitive billed input tokens across a batch.

Moving the invariant query digest into the system prompt enables cache writes/reads on the shared prefix, provided the prefix exceeds the model's minimum cacheable threshold (measured at 1024 tokens for claude-sonnet-4-6).

The hoisted prefix (system + query digest + orientation paragraph) measures 846 tokens, falling short of the 1024-token floor, resulting in zero cache activity and +936 input tokens (+5.8% regression) on the real corpus.
Judgment precision is preserved across the hoist: all 12 ordered-pair verdicts remain identical or shift only within sampling variance, with no relation changes between baseline and hoisted builds.
The sequential judge loop must warm the cache with a completed first call before any future parallelization fans out subsequent calls, to avoid converting 1 cache write into N premium writes.

The implementation relocates the query digest from volatile user message to cacheable system block via a shared_side keyword argument and orientation paragraph, with byte-identical behavior for calls omitting the argument.
